bullets.title: NVDA invests $3.5B in MediaTek; NVLink Fusion ecosystem expands
bullets.body: Nvidia announced a $3.5B convertible bond stake in MediaTek, with MediaTek adopting NVLink Fusion and NVHBM technologies. Multiple analysts frame this as Nvidia playing 'kingmaker' with next-gen ASIC partners (also MRVL), deepening ecosystem lock-in beyond GPUs—while posing a longer-term headwind to AVGO's custom XPU business. Jensen Huang stated the Vera Rubin platform generates '+$40B revenue per GW.'

bullets.title: Apple CEO transition: Tim Cook out, John Ternus in as of Sept 1
bullets.body: Tim Cook's 15-year tenure ended Aug 31; hardware chief John Ternus becomes CEO Sept 1, with Cook transitioning to executive chairman. Apple's market cap grew from ~$350B to nearly $4.7T under Cook—94% of current value created on his watch. Phil Schiller also resigned from App Store and events management roles simultaneously.

bullets.title: FTC files major ad-pricing antitrust suit against Amazon
bullets.body: The FTC, joined by 20+ state AGs, filed a complaint in Seattle federal court alleging Amazon deceived advertisers and manipulated ad prices on its retail platform, reaping 'tens of billions' over seven years. This is the third major FTC case against Amazon, following a prior $2.5B Prime settlement.

bullets.title: US 10-year yield tops 4.75%, 5-year hits 4.5%—highest since Jan 2025
bullets.body: Treasury yields surged to multi-year highs: 10-year at 4.756% (highest since Jan 13, 2025), 5-year at 4.5%. Move driven by TIPS weakness and oil surge from Iran tensions; Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks pushed September Fed hike odds to 54-62% per market pricing. Goldman's derivatives desk flagged the paradox that 'hawkish JH messaging' failed to lower long-end yields.

bullets.title: Mag 7 mostly lower premarket; NVDA only gainer at +0.6%
bullets.body: In premarket trading on Aug 31, Mag 7 stocks were broadly lower: MSFT -0.6%, TSLA -0.6%, GOOGL -0.5%, AMZN -0.4%, AAPL -0.3%, META -0.1%. NVDA bucked the trend, rising 0.6% after Friday's slide.

bullets.title: Anthropic valuation surge drove $150B in S&P 500 'other income'—GOOGL +$98B, AMZN +$53B
bullets.body: A widely-cited thread identified Anthropic's Q2 valuation jump from $380B to $965B as the driver of a $150B+ surge in S&P 500 aggregate earnings via 'other income'—contributing to reported 51% y/y earnings growth. GOOGL realized ~$98B and AMZN ~$53B from their Anthropic stakes; this 'circular financing' dynamic is described as 'the most bullish development for stock valuations in recent years' while simultaneously compressing Mag 7 forward P/E to near-decade lows.

bullets.title: MRVL at 100-day MA ahead of Oct 6 analyst day; CEO reserving key news
bullets.body: MRVL is trading at its 100-day moving average with analyst day on 10/6/26. CEO Murphy signaled key announcements will be reserved for the event rather than released at earnings. Separately, one analyst framed Celestial (MRVL acquisition) as potentially worth $6-10B as a standalone, with Q4 annualized revenue run rate of $500M and 2029 projection of $1B.

bullets.title: JPMorgan maintains bullish AVGO ahead of earnings; dismisses GOOGL TPU threat
bullets.body: JPMorgan maintained a bullish stance on AVGO heading into earnings, arguing AI business momentum is underestimated and market concerns about GOOGL TPU competition are overblown. Contrast with a separate Twitter analyst who sees NVDA's $3.5B MediaTek investment as eroding AVGO's competitive position longer-term.

bullets.title: TSLA most bullish options flow; BYD operating margin 5.4% vs TSLA 1.4%
bullets.body: TSLA had the most bullish options flow on the day and shares hit a one-week high, up 4.5%. However, a bear noted BYD's Q2 2026 operating margin of 5.4% versus TSLA's 1.4%, with TSLA expected to sell only 1.6M EVs in 2026—flat for a third consecutive year—as cheaper competitors constrain market share.

bullets.title: META on track to surpass Google Search in ad revenue by end-2026—Bernstein
bullets.body: Bernstein forecasts META will overtake Google Search in ad revenue by end of 2026, citing META capturing 'nearly half of every incremental digital ad dollar' in Q2. AI is cited as the primary accelerant of Meta's ad growth.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler: AMZN 'best positioned' for AI spending surge; $320 PT
bullets.body: Piper Sandler reiterated Overweight on Amazon with a $320 price target, calling it best positioned among major tech peers for the AI spending cycle, with expected 2026 ROIC around 14%.

bullets.title: TSMC unveils COUPE roadmap: AI compute 3x every 2 years, I/O only 1.4x—optical interconnects critical
bullets.body: At SEMICON Taiwan 2026, TSMC revealed AI compute capacity grows ~3x every two years while I/O bandwidth grows only ~1.4x, creating an 'I/O wall.' TSMC's advanced packaging VP forecasts silicon photonics market share exceeding 50% by 2027, with CPO (co-packaged optics) mass production beginning H2 2024. This structurally supports NVDA, COHR, LITE, MRVL, and AAOI in the bandwidth scaling trade.

bullets.title: Samsung locks 70% of memory capacity through 2031 via LTAs with NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL
bullets.body: Samsung Memory has reserved ~70% of production capacity through 2031 via long-term agreements, with NVDA, MSFT, and GOOGL as primary counterparties—five years of demand visibility. Samsung is also considering converting its Pyeongtaek S5 foundry line into memory capacity as early as next year.

bullets.title: INTC: SK Hynix clarifies it is NOT considering Intel Foundry for HBM4E base dies
bullets.body: Initial reports suggested SK Hynix was exploring dual-sourcing HBM4E base dies from TSM and Intel Foundry. SKHY subsequently clarified it is not currently considering Intel Foundry for HBM4E production. Separately, INTC expects advanced packaging (EMIB-T) revenue to ramp H2 2027 and reach stride by 2029.

bullets.title: RDDT and RBLX designated as 'Very Large' platforms under EU DSA
bullets.body: The European Commission designated Reddit and Roblox as 'Very Large Online Platforms' under the Digital Services Act, and ChatGPT as a 'Very Large Online Search Engine'—all now subject to stricter content moderation and compliance obligations.

bullets.title: AMD MI355X systems live in Saudi Arabia with Cisco networking via HUMAIN
bullets.body: AMD Instinct MI355X GPU-based AI infrastructure is now operational in Saudi Arabia, with Cisco Silicon One 800G networking. AMD, Cisco, and HUMAIN (PIF company) plan up to 250 MW of AI infrastructure deployment by 2027.

bullets.title: CRM up 50% since Chamath's May 15 SaaS comeback call; enterprise SoR rerating underway
bullets.body: Salesforce has rallied 50% since Chamath issued a bullish SaaS call on May 15. A separate weekly note flagged enterprise segment-of-responsibility rerating as rational, with AIDC demand running at 2x deliverable supply and MRVL optics driving the raise—while software-to-semis/hardware divergence widens.

bullets.title: Goldman vol desk: risk-reward for upside 'extremely compelling' despite seasonal stress
bullets.body: Goldman's top volatility trader said risk-reward for owning upside is 'extremely compelling' despite seasonal headwinds. Counter-intuitively, call skews are at highs while put skews are at lows per GS data, and millions in further-dated SPY call buys with concurrent put sales suggest bullish positioning by large players.

bullets.title: S&P 500 cycle composite entering historically most challenging seasonal stretch
bullets.body: The NDR S&P 500 Cycle Composite—blending one-year seasonal, four-year presidential, and 10-year decennial cycles—is now entering what it identifies as the most challenging stretch of the year historically. SPY has been down 0.7% since Aug 4 after a 5.74% rally July 29-Aug 4.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño chip removes L2 cache; ad business hits $1B annualized run rate
bullets.body: OpenAI's custom 'Jalapeño' chip removes L2 cache to cut inference latency, addressing the 'operands arrive late' problem via NUMA-style local HBM architecture. Separately, OpenAI's advertising business hit $1B annualized revenue, with advertisers now able to purchase ChatGPT ads directly via an ads manager rolling out in India, Europe, Middle East, and North Africa.
